clue.text: Help round to summit, as it were

indicators.note: the distress call is placed around the next word, enclosing it

parts.note: SOS is the international call for help
taken as written
a summit is a peak

explanation.surface: A climber gets help reaching the top, or something like it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'round' is the container signal: the distress call wraps the word 'to'. 'Help' looks like a verb but stands for the call itself.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are hedging idioms used to show a phrase is not meant literally.

clue.text: One swimmer

definitions.meaning: ... as an adjective means only or single

explanation.surface: A lone figure in the water.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is the adjective meaning single or only; the other is a flatfish.

clue.text: Net split from below

indicators.note: in a down clue, reading from below means the word is read upwards, backwards

parts.note: to split is to part

explanation.surface: A net torn open from underneath.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from below' reads PART upwards in this down answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A net is a device for catching animals, as is a snare.

clue.text: Nuisance also seen in fair

indicators.note: the word for also appears inside the word for fair

parts.note: so-so means middling, fair
and means also, in addition

explanation.surface: An annoying person turns up at a funfair as well.
explanation.walkthrough: 'seen in' is the container signal. 'fair' means middling here, not a funfair.
explanation.definitionFit: A so-and-so is a euphemism for an irritating, unpleasant person.

clue.text: Entering rising river, female pretty and delicate

indicators.note: the abbreviation for female goes into the river's name
in a down clue, rising means the river's name is read upwards

parts.note: the Nile is the great river of Egypt

explanation.surface: A pretty girl wades into a river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rising' turns NILE into ELIN; 'Entering' puts F inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Elfin describes someone small, slight and delicately attractive, like a fairy creature.

clue.text: Little inclination to conceal intelligence, a smart alec

indicators.note: the small hill hides the other letters inside it

parts.note: a knoll is a small hill, a little slope
wit means intelligence, good sense

explanation.surface: A clever clogs has little desire to hide how bright they are.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Little inclination' is a small hill, not a weak urge; 'to conceal' makes it a container holding the wordplay's other pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Both terms describe someone who boasts of knowing everything; smart alec is a mild insult.

clue.text: Copper pen in 3-D

parts.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper
Bic is a well-known brand of ballpoint pen

explanation.surface: A copper pen drawn in three dimensions.
explanation.definitionFit: Cubic means having three dimensions, like volume measured in length, breadth and height.

clue.text: Meaner race, it's going off round Thai capital

indicators.note: the jumbled letters go round the leading letter of the next word
going off means going wrong, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
read as 'it is': IT, with the 's as a link

indicators.note: a capital is the head letter of the word Thai

explanation.surface: A spiteful contest goes wrong around Bangkok.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going off' is the anagram signal and 'round' the container; 'capital' means the first letter of Thai, not Bangkok.
explanation.definitionFit: Catty means spiteful, so cattier is a comparative synonym of meaner.

clue.text: As hurricane may be described in every detail?

definitions.meaning: a hurricane comes in one gust after another
a ... account covers events step by step

explanation.surface: A storm report covering every gust.
explanation.definitionFit: A full account gives each event in turn; literally, a hurricane is gust after gust.

clue.text: Arrive guarding soldiers with rubbish report

indicators.note: the word for arrive surrounds the other letters, protecting them

parts.note: to arrive is to come
men is a crossword stock word for soldiers
tat is cheap rubbish

explanation.surface: Someone arrives with troops and a scathing report.
explanation.walkthrough: 'guarding' is the container signal, with the arrival word on the outside.
explanation.definitionFit: To commentate is to give a running description of events, as a sports broadcaster does.

clue.text: Originally, lama is blessed with a place in Tibet

indicators.note: originally points at the opening letter of lama

parts.note: to be blessed with something is to have it

explanation.surface: A holy man is fortunate to have a home in Tibet.
explanation.definitionFit: Lhasa is the capital city of Tibet.

clue.text: Move or not from anterior chamber

indicators.note: the instruction to move these letters reorders them

explanation.surface: Someone is told to move, or not, out of the front of the building.
explanation.definitionFit: Anterior means at the front, and a chamber is a room.

clue.text: Horribly inedible fat I easily picked out

indicators.note: horribly suggests the letters are mangled into another order

explanation.surface: A diner spots the gristly fat on their plate at once.
explanation.definitionFit: Something identifiable can be recognised, so it stands out easily.

clue.text: Central American fellow actor, trust me!

parts.note: a co-star shares the bill with another actor
'I can' is a confident reassurance, as in trust me to do it

explanation.surface: An actor reassures a castmate about a role.
explanation.definitionFit: Costa Rica is a country in Central America; its people are Central Americans.

clue.text: Give it everything, O frog?

parts.note: the letters of '... up give these words, so a wordplay of GO FOR plus a word meaning smashed would produce them

explanation.surface: A plea to a frog to make every effort.
explanation.walkthrough: A reverse clue: BROKE as an anagram signal applied to GO FOR yields 'O frog'.
explanation.definitionFit: To go for broke is an idiom meaning to risk all in a total effort.

clue.text: Principal of university accessing revolving door, so fragrant

indicators.note: the leading letter gets in among the turned letters
revolving suggests the letters spin into a new order
the principal, first, letter of the word university

explanation.surface: A college head enters through a revolving door into a sweet smell.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revolving' scrambles the door and 'so' together, not just a reversal; 'accessing' slips the university's first letter in near the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Odorous means having a smell, here a pleasant one, so it matches scented.

clue.text: Starting price fairly active

parts.note: SP is the betting abbreviation for starting price
rightly means justly, fairly

explanation.surface: The odds on a horse are pretty lively.
explanation.definitionFit: Sprightly means lively and energetic, an apt synonym for active.

clue.text: Nick entertained by a short musical circus performer

indicators.note: the word for nick is taken inside the shortened show
short means the last letter is cut off

parts.note: Cats is the Andrew Lloyd Webber musical
to nick is to steal, to rob

explanation.surface: A thief is welcomed at a brief stage show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short' clips the final letter of the Lloyd Webber show; 'entertained by' makes it a container for the theft word.
explanation.definitionFit: An acrobat performs tumbling and trapeze feats, a classic circus act.

clue.text: Drink sent over for chum

indicators.note: sent over means turned over, reading the word backwards

parts.note: to lap is to drink, as a cat does

explanation.surface: A drink is sent across to a friend.
explanation.definitionFit: Pal and chum are both informal words for a friend.

clue.text: Soldier on, bad time to retreat

indicators.note: retreating means going backwards, so the letters are read in reverse

parts.note: re means on, concerning
poor means bad, inferior

explanation.surface: A soldier carries on although it is a bad moment to pull back.
explanation.definitionFit: A trooper is a private soldier, especially in a cavalry or armoured unit.

clue.text: Particular recipes rewritten

indicators.note: writing again lets the letters come out in a new order

explanation.surface: A fussy cook has the recipes redone.
explanation.definitionFit: Particular can mean exact or meticulous, the same as precise.

clue.text: Strike yobbo gripping wood

indicators.note: the word for yobbo holds the tree inside it

parts.note: a yobbo is a lout, a British word for an uncouth youth
ash is a wood, from the ash tree

explanation.surface: A thug holding a club hits out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gripping' is the container signal. Yobbo is British slang for an uncouth young man.
explanation.definitionFit: To lash out is to strike suddenly and violently.

clue.text: Template for drawing nicest wavy line

indicators.note: wavy suggests a twisted, rearranged form of the letters

explanation.surface: An artist's guide for a nice wavy line.
explanation.definitionFit: A stencil is a cut-out sheet used as a guide to reproduce a design.

clue.text: Couple stretched when working in theatre?

definitions.text: Couple stretched when working in theatre?

parts.words: Couple stretched when working in theatre?
parts.note: a pair of stretchy items pulled on by surgeons in the operating theatre, with theatre misleading towards the stage

explanation.surface: Actors exhausted after a long run on stage.
explanation.walkthrough: Theatre here is a hospital operating theatre, not a playhouse.
explanation.definitionFit: Surgeons wear a pair of these elastic hand coverings during operations.

clue.text: Descriptive of galley, a shade beneath surface of ocean

indicators.note: in a down clue the shade and a sit below the top letter
the surface, top, letter of ocean

parts.note: red is a shade, a colour

explanation.surface: A galley sits in reddish water just under the sea's surface.
explanation.definitionFit: A galley was a ship propelled by oars, so it can be called oared.

clue.text: In Vietnam, a lively country

indicators.note: in signals the answer is contained within the following words

explanation.surface: A lively time in Vietnam.
explanation.definitionFit: Mali is a landlocked country in West Africa.

clue.text: Closely fitting items to stick to, upside down

indicators.note: in a down clue, upside down means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: from the idiom stick to your guns, meaning hold firm

explanation.surface: Tight clothing, with things to cling to, worn inverted.
explanation.definitionFit: Snug describes a garment that fits tightly and comfortably.

clue.text: Poor or richest singer

indicators.note: poor suggests the letters are in a bad state, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A singer, whether poor or wealthy.
explanation.definitionFit: A chorister sings in a choir, so is a type of singer.

clue.text: Cuppa in range

parts.note: cha is a British slang word for tea, a cuppa

explanation.surface: A cup of tea within reach.
explanation.walkthrough: Cuppa is British for a cup of tea.
explanation.definitionFit: A chain of mountains is a range.

clue.text: Relative peace ultimately in Riviera city

indicators.note: the final letter goes into the city's name

parts.note: Nice is a city on the French Riviera

indicators.note: ultimately points at the final letter of peace

explanation.surface: A family member finds calm in a resort on the Côte d'Azur.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ultimately' takes E; 'in' puts it inside NICE.
explanation.definitionFit: A niece is a family member, a sibling's daughter.

clue.text: Swiss singing almost weird in loud performance?

indicators.note: the shortened word goes inside the loud performance

parts.note: yelling is a loud vocal performance, as the question mark admits

indicators.note: almost means the last letter is dropped

parts.note: odd means weird

explanation.surface: Alpine singing that sounds strange and noisy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' clips the last letter of the word for weird and 'in' places it inside; the question mark admits the loose definition of shouting.
explanation.definitionFit: Yodelling is the warbling vocal style traditional in the Swiss Alps.
